title: ObjectSchema
description: A schema node of type 'object' that constrains JSON object instances by declaring a set of named, typed properties, which of those properties must be present, and rules for undeclared or dynamically named keys. In code it is a declaration that only states such a shape: a TypeScript interface or object type alias; a record, struct, dataclass or data class of named, typed fields with at most generated or trivial accessors and constructors; an entity class or ORM model whatever the framework; or an object entry in a JSON Schema, OpenAPI or validator definition. An interface or type that declares state fields beside callbacks that read or write that state (the state and actions of a client-side store, a context value, a record that carries a handler) is still an object schema: it types one value, and the callbacks are members of that value. A declaration is an object schema whether or not its shape is persisted or published: it records that values are held to a stated shape. Names such as data transfer object (DTO), view model, API model or read model say what a shape is used for, not what kind of thing it is: the values that travel have the schema, the declaration in code is where that schema is written down, and the model records the declaration as the object schema and its use as relationships from the elements that use it (the application service, function or event that accesses it). It is not an individual field or a primitive type alias. Use application DataObject instead when the class is a domain object rather than only a shape: it also has methods of its own that validate, derive from or change its fields (a value object, an aggregate held in memory) and it is not a persisted entity, or the data is handled with no declared shape at all; an object schema may realize such a data object. Use application ApplicationEvent instead when the record is named for an occurrence and is published to a bus or dispatched to handlers, even though it declares only fields. Use application ApplicationService instead when the interface declares operations as a contract that one or more classes implement and callers depend on in place of an implementation (a service, repository or dependency-injection contract), whether or not it also exposes properties; an interface that types one value and declares that value's state beside callbacks over it stays an object schema. Use apm LogRecord instead when the declared shape is that of an entry the system writes to a log, wherever the log is kept. Use SchemaProperty instead when the symbol is a single field, column or attribute inside a structure rather than the structure that owns the fields. Use JSONSchema instead when the element is the root schema document or file, identified by $schema and $id and holding definitions, rather than one object shape described within it. Use SchemaDefinition instead when the named reusable type is a primitive alias or enumeration (e.g. a TypeScript enum, a branded string type, a Python Enum) with no named fields of its own. Use SchemaComposition instead when the type is defined only by combining other schemas (union, intersection, discriminated oneOf, negation) rather than by declaring its own properties; plain class inheritance stays an objectschema with a specializes relationship.

type.description: The JSON Schema type keyword, which is always the string 'object' for this element; set it on every instance.

properties.description: Named property definitions for the object schema (primary mechanism for defining object structure)

patternProperties.description: Pattern-matched property definitions applied to properties whose names match the given regex

propertyNames.description: Schema applied to all property names of the object instance for name validation

required.description: Array of property names (strings) that must be present in a valid instance; populate it from fields that are non-optional in code, such as TypeScript fields without '?', Pydantic fields without defaults, or NOT NULL columns.

additionalProperties.description: Either a boolean or a subschema (inline or $ref) governing keys not listed in properties or patternProperties; set false for closed models (e.g. Pydantic extra='forbid', TypeScript exact types) and a value schema for map-like types such as Record<string, T>. This schema stores the value as a single string.

minProperties.description: Non-negative integer giving the minimum number of keys a valid instance must contain; set it only when code or a validator explicitly enforces a lower bound on key count.

maxProperties.description: Non-negative integer giving the maximum number of keys a valid instance may contain; set it only when code or a validator explicitly enforces an upper bound on key count.

x-dr-standard: JSON Schema Draft 7 Validation (draft-handrews-json-schema-validation-01) §6.5 Validation Keywords for Objects
x-dr-evidence: A class annotated @Entity/@Table, a Django models.Model subclass, or a SQLAlchemy declarative class whose attributes declare domain fields

A TypeScript interface or object type alias, a Go or Rust struct, a Java or C# record, a Kotlin data class, a Python @dataclass, TypedDict or NamedTuple, or a Lombok @Data class or plain property class whose declaration is only named typed fields, whatever it types (an API payload, a DTO, a view model, store state, a function's parameters or its result); or a Pydantic BaseModel or other validation model
A JSON Schema or OpenAPI components.schemas entry with "type": "object" and a "properties" map, or a z.object()/Joi.object()/yup.object() validator declaration

An interface or type that types one store or context value: state fields beside function-typed members that set, toggle, reset or select that state (the state-and-actions type passed to a store factory, the value type of a UI context), implemented by one object rather than by classes behind a contract
